A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KOCO-SMC and its Upper-Lower Watch algorithm. The main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original solver evaluations, an ULW ablation, supply-chain and delivery experiments, and additional runtime and compilation results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark, ablation, and application results, revises the approximate-solver evaluation, and includes additional runtime results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The core CDCL framework and ULW bound recurrences remain. However, v2 Algorithm 1 places Boolean propagation before probabilistic checks, and Appendix C specifies skipping satisfied probabilistic constraints until backtracking. v1 instead describes continued watched-variable updates and explicitly avoids removing satisfied constraints.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 50 binary UAI models, nine grid-coloring formulas, 20/28/44-node supply networks, and 8/18/24-location delivery graphs. Despite revised application prose and illustrations, v2 Appendix D.4 retains the original supply-chain budget constraints. Threshold changes concern evaluation settings rather than new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: XOR-SMC, Gibbs-SAA, BP-SAA, and the exact SAT/inference combinations are retained. SAT-* becomes Lingeling-* in several figures; MiniSAT and CaDiCaL combinations already appeared in v1 Figure 3. Newly cited bounding and stochastic-optimization methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The approximate comparison changes from nine normalized thresholds spanning 10^-35 to 10^5 to three thresholds, 10^-20, 10^-10, and 10^-1. v2 specifies exact verification and four outcome categories, and its main text changes the budget from one hour to ten minutes. Appendices D.2-D.3 still specify one hour, leaving the executed budget unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds substantial failure analysis: correct, wrong, unverifiable, and timed-out outcomes, separated according to whether KOCO-SMC solves the instances. This replaces the earlier aggregate solved-rate analysis. The ULW ablation, compilation-time analysis, and two application studies remain.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.2 expands repeated-run reporting beyond the existing any-correct-run success rule, specifying how all-wrong, unfinished, and otherwise unverifiable runs determine an instance's category. Both appendices still specify five runs; no increase in runs, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing is established.

E6.justification: v1 Figures 1(right) and 5 are replaced by new outcome distributions in v2 Figures 1(right) and 4. These report incorrect and unverifiable answers and cases where approximate solvers answer instances that time out for KOCO-SMC. The changed protocols prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains. Exact-solver, ULW, and appendix runtime results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B supplies the missing product-node bound inequality and presents the argument explicitly as induction. Section 3.1 also changes the illustrative learned clause to include the predicate b1. The ULW lemma, smoothness/decomposability assumptions, and central bound construction otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The efficient exact-solver and ULW contributions remain. v2 removes the headline claim of solving 40% more hard instances, acknowledges occasional advantages of approximate solvers, and changes the contribution statement from superiority in both quality and efficiency to quality or efficiency.

C2.justification: The approximate-solver comparison receives a substantially more qualified interpretation: KOCO-SMC can time out where approximate methods return answers, unverifiable answers are distinguished from incorrect ones, and XOR-SMC's difficulties are linked to the SAT-UNSAT transition and approximation bounds. v2 also explicitly limits its methodological focus to threshold-form probabilistic constraints.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit project repository link and documents the three default benchmark thresholds. Conversely, it removes Algorithm 2, detailed watcher management, VSIDS and first-UIP explanations, explicit Hamiltonian-path CNF clauses, and the travel-order treatment of time. These materially change the available implementation guidance, although hardware and most baseline hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning against DPLL-based bounds, marginal-MAP bounding, and stochastic constraint optimization, including new discussions of Dubray, Ge and Biere, and Latour's work. The introduction also reframes the exact comparators as constructed baselines in the absence of general exact SMC solvers, replacing v1's existing-solvers framing.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting affects the introduction, method explanations, experimental interpretation, and applications. The appendices are reorganized into separate inference, proof, implementation, settings, and results sections; Algorithm 1 moves into the main text. The title, contribution presentation, acknowledgements, and impact statement also change.

P2.justification: The main text adopts a two-column layout with extensively rearranged figures. Approximate-solver charts become stacked outcome displays; supply-chain and delivery illustrations are redrawn, and the delivery map and traffic schematic are consolidated. Circuit examples are rearranged, while retained runtime plots receive new placement, legends, or styling.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the central comparison by distinguishing incorrect from unverifiable answers and acknowledging approximate solvers' occasional advantages, making the claims better calibrated. Expanded related-work positioning and explicit code access also help assessment. These gains are limited by the unresolved ten-minute versus one-hour protocol discrepancy and the removal of useful implementation and task-encoding details.
